parsed.attack: Nobody in the evidence asked for this: [222] is teachers hand-importing curriculum decks mid-semester, and the leap from that to social facts about colleagues is the author's, not any user's. The failure mode of relationship memory is also misdiagnosed - you do remember that your neighbour's mother is ill the moment you see your neighbour; what fails is acting, and retrieving the fact at 6am inside a deck with no neighbour present produces recall without occasion. Teachers guard the morning review because it serves a professional goal, and the observed behaviour of experienced SRS users is aggressive pruning of cards that do not earn their slot.
parsed.strongest_defence: There is genuine revealed behaviour immediately adjacent to this - people already build decks to learn names and faces, and a teacher facing 150 new students each September has a concrete, seasonal, professional reason to do it - so the mechanic is not invented; only the relationship-maintenance framing is.
parsed.verdict_reason: The only evidenced demand here is name-and-face learning for a professional reason, and the friendship framing the idea is sold on has no observed user behind it.
